speaker: A. A. Kirillov
title: Affine sl(2), the principal Heisenberg algebra, and vertex operators
summary: Kirillov explains the Lepowsky--Wilson realization of the basic affine \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\)-module. Gelfand interrupts with generators and relations, root monomials, Heisenberg subalgebras and possible analogies with paths, \(p\)-adic algebra and quadratic forms. The actual mathematical entry occupies P001026--P001029; the catalogue range overlaps Zamolodchikov, whose heading begins P001030. The loop cocycle, central generator and oscillator indices require explicit normalization corrections. The 1978 published construction makes the principal line expository in September 1982.

speaker: A. B. Zamolodchikov
title: Classical string constraints and cyclic invariant charges
summary: The entry proper begins on P001030 and ends with the first lines of P001033. It moves from the Nambu--Goto action and Dirac constraints through two Witt algebras to oscillator quantization and the Virasoro anomaly. It then asks for the quantum algebra of cyclic iterated integrals. The classical construction, the asserted invariance of naively normally ordered operators, abstract deformation quantization, and completeness are distinct items with different later fates.

speaker: A. S. Schwarz
title: Gauge symmetry, topological strings and mirror particles
summary: The actual entry occupies P001033--P001036. A discussion of subjects to study leads to gauge covariantization, symmetry breaking and vacuum topology. Schwarz then describes strings whose holonomy reverses electric charge or exchanges ordinary and mirror matter. The printed group-theoretic criterion lacks a crucial stabilizer hypothesis. The final quantum-stability question and astrophysical anecdotes do not specify enough data for an independently identifiable theorem.

speaker: Ya. G. Sinai
title: Period doubling, renormalization and period tripling
summary: On P001037 Sinai proposes physics topics and then discusses Feigenbaum universality; Migdal adds further agenda items. Sinai's mathematics ends midway down P001038. The entry gives period-doubling scaling, robustness of suitable families, a suggested flow extension, complex period tripling and the renormalization fixed-point equation. Numerical approximation is distinguished from a validated proof, and the broad post-accumulation question is not treated as a uniquely defined open problem.

speaker: A. A. Migdal
title: Stochastic quantization and reduction to large random matrices
summary: The mathematical entry starts on the lower half of P001038 after Sinai and ends on P001040. It develops Langevin quantization, factorization of normalized traces, quenched momenta and reduction of a matrix field to finitely many matrices. The definite calculation requested is the all-coupling large-\(N\) free energy of four unitary matrices. The manuscript retains a negative exponent and all ordered index pairs; those conventions are essential to the development. The one-matrix external-field integral at the end is a separate already studied model.

speaker: D. B. Fuchs
title: Virasoro Verma modules and semi-infinite exterior powers
summary: The actual entry occupies P001041--P001042. Fuchs presents the central extension of circle vector fields, Verma modules, tensor-density modules and their semi-infinite exterior powers, then the Kac determinant criterion and a second oscillator construction. The explicitly cited Feigin--Fuchs paper had appeared in the second issue of 1982. The notebook reverses two signs, omits commutator factors, and writes operators which are not the required Heisenberg modes; these defects are separated from the valid representation-theoretic content.

speaker: A. B. Zamolodchikov
title: From random paths to Polyakov sums over surfaces
summary: The entry begins on P001043 and ends above the 4 October heading on P001046. Classical area and conformal coordinates lead into three path regularizations: lattice walks, fixed-length random rods, and Gaussian increments. Their properly normalized diffusive limits motivate the intrinsic-metric integral for surfaces. Several formulas omit scaling factors, and the passage from fixed-metric Gaussian fields to a sum over geometries remains a formal construction.

speaker: A. A. Kirillov
title: Springer resolution and limiting orbital integrals
summary: The entry occupies the middle and lower part of P001046 and the first lines of P001047. Kirillov reports Ginzburg\textquotesingle s work after explaining adjoint orbits and Springer resolution. The 1983 paper identifies the nilpotent-orbit limit formula precisely for complex semisimple algebras regarded as real. Gelfand then asks how a singular hyperbola integral recovers the value of a test function at the crossing.

speaker: A. B. Zamolodchikov
title: From path entropy to the Polyakov metric integral and Liouville theory
summary: The actual entry starts halfway through P001047 and ends on P001049. Zamolodchikov reviews the proper-time representation of a particle path sum, then the fixed-topology Polyakov metric integral, quotienting by reparametrizations, functional metrics, conformal gauge and the Liouville action. The uncertainty about summing over handles is separate from the fixed-topology calculation. Several expressions are formal prescriptions: neither an infinite-dimensional Riemannian metric nor division by a gauge-group volume by itself constructs a measure.

speaker: V. L. Ginzburg
title: Coisotropic reduction, canonical projectors and double fibrations
summary: The actual entry occupies P001050 and the upper part of P001051, before Fröhlich. The catalogue attribution to V. L. Ginzburg is retained; the notebook gives only V. Ginzburg and explicitly presents the material after Guillemin--Sternberg. The full speaker identity has not been independently resolved from another dated seminar source. V. A. Ginzburg’s 1983 paper is used for mathematical comparison, without identifying its author as this speaker. The talk relates a regular coisotropic quotient to a symmetric idempotent canonical relation and an operator algebra, then Shmelyov gives the conormal embedding condition for a double fibration.

speaker: J. Fröhlich
title: Nonminimal monopoles, four-manifold topology, and Witten’s Morse deformation
summary: The entry begins midway down P001051 after Ginzburg and ends on P001054. Fröhlich reports Taubes, Donaldson and Witten, with a final announcement about Enss. The notes distinguish small from zero eigenvalues, but their deformed differential changes sign between pages, their oscillator loses diagonal terms, and its ground state loses the Gaussian. The reconstructions keep the monopole sector, regularity of instanton moduli and long-range scattering modifiers explicit.

speaker: J. Fröhlich
title: Random lattice surfaces, roughening, and the proposed Regge continuum limit
summary: The mathematical entry occupies P001055--P001057. The first model is an integer-valued solid-on-solid height graph with a rigorous roughening result; the later questions concern more general plaquette surfaces and their topology. A closely matching 1982 primary lecture text makes this distinction explicit. Boundary-independent exponential growth was developed in a 1983 paper by the speaker and collaborators, but neither a power-law correction nor a general continuum-limit theorem follows from it. The final Regge curvature theorem is kept separate from the proposed convergence of random-metric integrals.

speaker: A. B. Zamolodchikov
title: Primary fields, Virasoro degeneracy, and the Liouville spectrum
summary: The entry begins on P001058 and ends on P001059; the broader catalogue range includes the preceding surface lecture and following Beilinson record. Zamolodchikov asks how to compute primary-field matrix elements and which highest-weight modules have null states; Neretin supplies the reducibility criterion. The second half returns to the independent-metric string integral, the Liouville action, a cylinder evolution kernel and a conjectural Virasoro description of the spectrum. These are distinct questions: BPZ develops the correlator program in 1984, whereas a much later spectral theorem gives a rigorous real-coupling Liouville realization. Several notebook formulas require consistent mode conventions or substantive emendations.

speaker: A. A. Beilinson
title: Regular singular D-modules and gluing
summary: The actual entry begins on P001060, after the preceding Liouville discussion. Gelfand recalls the Lorentz-group reduction to linear algebra; Beilinson then describes regular singular modules on a punctured disk and gluing across a closed subvariety. The final relation \(vu=N\) is shorthand, not a complete definition. Beilinson’s later paper explicitly says it follows S. I. Gelfand’s 1982 notes \citep[introduction]{beilinson1987glue}.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Continuous-dimensional Grassmannians and a Schubert analogy
summary: The intervention occupies the top of P001061. Gelfand recalls finite Grassmannian cells, then asks about fixed-trace projections in a type \(\mathrm{II}_1\) factor, continuous flags, monotone parameters, topology and cohomology. The notebook expressly calls the problem imprecise, so these questions are preserved as a programme rather than assigned a fabricated solved/open theorem.

speaker: Yu. I. Manin
title: Twistor geometry and flag superspaces
summary: The entry occupies P001061--P001063. After an agenda extending to supersymmetric field equations, Manin recalls the Grassmannian model of compactified complex Minkowski space, formulates a classification problem for flag superspaces, and explains the functor of points and two examples. The surviving text stops at the opening of the Penrose correspondence; it contains no worked new Yang--Mills solution. The closely related 1983 chapter is identifiable, but its full classification has not been verified here \citep{manin1983flags}.

speaker: A. M. Polyakov
title: Liouville uniformization, accessory parameters and Virasoro blocks
summary: The talk occupies P001064--P001069. It moves from the Liouville action and cusp uniformization to the stress tensor, accessory parameters, and the proposed recovery of classical geometry from quantum Ward identities. The last pages give a Verma-module expansion and an oscillator realization. The classical generating-function conjecture was proved by Zograf and Takhtajan; the conformal-block programme appears in BPZ 1984, while rigorous sphere Liouville construction and bootstrap came much later. Several factors, powers and completeness relations in the notebook are inconsistent and are explicitly corrected below.

speaker: I. Yu. Kobzarev
title: Domain walls, vortex strings and the Nambu action
summary: The actual talk is P001070--P001073. A scalar double well supplies a planar wall; the Abelian Higgs model supplies a vortex string. Integrating a thin core yields the Nambu worldsheet action, with a collapsing circular loop as an illustration. The final page introduces the colour gauge Lagrangian. These are expository constructions predating the talk; the wall formula can be checked against Kobzarev’s own 1974 paper. The notes suppress couplings and contain a gauge-sign mismatch.

title: Year 1983
summary: This MCCME record is a year heading. It has no separate mathematical content; the adjacent February material belongs to records 580 and 581.

speaker: A. A. Kirillov
title: Near-unitary circle actions and Fock-space representations
summary: The record occupies the upper part of P001074. Following Gelfand’s methodological and supersymmetry remarks, Kirillov reports Neretin’s weighted pullbacks, their Hilbert--Schmidt failure of unitarity, and Gaussian/Fock unitarization. This construction had already appeared in 1982; extending the action on the original one-particle space and constructing a new unitary action on Fock space must be distinguished \citep{neretin1982complementary}.

speaker: B. L. Feigin
title: String constraints and semi-infinite homology
summary: The actual notes occupy the lower P001074 and P001075. They pass from the loop-space symplectic form to oscillator quantization, explain the central-term obstruction to ordinary invariants, and replace invariants by the image of positive-mode invariants in negative-mode coinvariants. Feigin’s 1984 note identifies this physical-state construction with semi-infinite homology. Gelfand’s closing p-adic request has a separately documented answer in Neretin’s 1984 paper.

speaker: Yu. A. Neretin
title: Hilbert transforms, almost invariant kernels and circle representations
summary: The entry is P001076--P001077, including a name of Ginzburg crossed out before the final continuation question. The 1982 near-orthogonal construction is refined by endpoint complex structures and restricted symplectic actions, published in Neretin’s 1983 Doklady note. Gelfand’s pseudodifferential generalization remains unspecified. The written logarithmic convolution cannot yield the claimed derivative of a delta distribution; the Fock-space question needs a completed symmetric space rather than arbitrary analytic sequences.

speaker: V. L. Ginzburg
title: Duistermaat--Heckman localization and orbital integrals
summary: The entry occupies P001078 and the upper part of P001079. It presents Hamiltonian torus actions, regular reduction, affine variation of reduced symplectic classes, polynomial densities and exact stationary phase, then relates these to convexity and characters. The 1982 theorem is expository here. The nonisolated fixed-component formula is abbreviated beyond validity: normal-bundle curvature terms are needed. The historical allusions to Semenov-Tian-Shansky and Vergne have identifiable pre-talk sources.

speaker: A. A. Kirillov
title: The SU(3) orbit hexagon and weight multiplicities
summary: The intervention begins in the lower part of P001079 and ends with a single request on P001080. It revisits the six-dimensional regular orbit, its torus-moment hexagon and changes in the fibers. The written map uses two conjugacy invariants and therefore cannot produce that hexagon; diagonal projection is the required interpretation. The final weight-multiplicity request recurs from 1981-556 and retains GP-1981-41.

speaker: V. I. Arnold
title: Mathieu gaps, Catalan diagrams and spectral perturbation
summary: The actual talk is P001081--P001086; P001080 belongs to Kirillov and P001087 begins Krichever. Arnold explains delayed splitting of Hill eigenvalues for trigonometric-polynomial perturbations by quiver paths, Catalan bracket fillings and a reversal involution. The paper received on 1 February 1983 and published later that year closely matches the talk. Its 30 March supplement acknowledges older results of Bloch, Levy--Keller and Hochstadt, so the estimates and coefficient identities are not all classified as new 1983 discoveries. Gelfand’s one-gap question remains underdetermined in this record.

speaker: I. M. Krichever
title: Hessians and perturbations of finite gap KdV solutions
summary: The actual notes start on P001087 and end above Wodzicki\textquotesingle s heading on P001089. They describe the spectral diagonalization of a stationary KdV Hessian and a basis for first order perturbation theory; Gelfand asks for higher variations. The catalogue range includes the end of Arnold and the start of Wodzicki.

speaker: Mariusz Wodzicki
title: Finite gap Hill zeta functions and regularized determinants
summary: From the lower part of P001089 through P001092, Wodzicki presents zeta values for finite gap Hill operators, universal polynomials, and a Lam\'e example. Interventions concern elementary zeta values, arithmetic, determinant multiplicativity, and a Clausen-series formula. The core became a three-page 1984 paper; the peripheral questions have different evidentiary status.

speaker: S. P. Novikov
title: Many-valued actions and transgression
summary: The talk occupies P001093 and the upper part of P001094. It constructs a globally defined variation from locally defined action functionals, illustrated by the Dirac monopole and mapping spaces. The 1982 survey is already a pre-talk source.

speaker: M. A. Semenov-Tian-Shansky
title: Classical r-matrices and factorization
summary: From the second heading on P001094 through P001095 the notes introduce an operator \(R\), two Lie--Poisson brackets, invariant Hamiltonians, modified Yang--Baxter identities and factorization. Gelfand asks for the \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) classification. The final quadratic bracket anticipates the exact 1983 article.

speaker: Mariusz Wodzicki
title: APS boundary index theory and local spectral invariants
summary: The actual record is P001096--P001098. It reviews all three Atiyah--Patodi--Singer papers, includes Fedosov\textquotesingle s symbol-projector construction, and connects heat coefficients, eta regularity and secondary invariants. Gelfand asks about formal cohomology of metrics and symbols. Several questions recur verbatim in the 1981--82 index.

speaker: George Wilson
title: Loop Grassmannians, integrable flows, and the tau function
summary: The actual record is P001099--P001100. Wilson announces joint work with Segal and relates loop groups, Grassmannians, KdV, modified KdV, determinant lines and affine central extensions. Krichever adds the zero-curvature KP interpretation. This is the prospectus for the detailed April lecture.

speaker: George Wilson
title: The determinant tau function and the KP Grassmannian
summary: P001101--P001107 gives the detailed Segal--Wilson construction: frames and determinants, Schur expansions, algebraic curves, Baker functions and Miwa shifts, formal Lax equations, determinant-line extensions, and local Miura factorizations. Gelfand\textquotesingle s broad request about theta functions of all abelian varieties is kept separate from the precise Jacobian results.

speaker: George Wilson
title: KP and its scalar reductions: concluding note
summary: Only the lower strip of P001108 belongs to this brief conclusion. It repeats the formal KP hierarchy and its scalar differential reductions, and identifies \(2q_1\) as a KP solution. Ginzburg begins on the next page.

speaker: V. L. Ginzburg
title: Equivariant localization and the Duistermaat–Heckman theorem
summary: The actual report occupies P001109--P001112, after Wilson\textquotesingle s conclusion on P001108. It compares the Duistermaat--Heckman theorem, the Atiyah--Bott equivariant interpretation, Witten\textquotesingle s parity complex, and the explicit primitive attributed to Vergne. The last page records a successful correction of an initially impossible closed angular form.

speaker: V. L. Ginzburg
title: Moment-map convexity and density chambers
summary: The actual report is the upper and middle portion of P001113, ending at Beilinson\textquotesingle s heading. A preceding plan mentions reading Levinson on the zeta function but supplies no theorem. P001115 starts 5 September 1983 and belongs to the next academic year, despite the catalogue overlap.

speaker: A. A. Beilinson
title: Arithmetic zeta functions and the global continuation problem
summary: The talk starts in the lower portion of P001113 and continues on P001114, with a short Wodzicki interruption before Beilinson resumes. The heading promises special values up to a rational factor and exact formulations, but the recorded mathematics concerns local factors, global continuation, a Langlands-type correspondence, and the elliptic functional equation. No rank or leading-coefficient formula for Birch--Swinnerton-Dyer is actually recorded.

speaker: Mariusz Wodzicki
title: Shintani-type zeta series and a proposed operator realization
summary: This is the short interruption in the middle of P001114, between Beilinson\textquotesingle s strong correspondence conjecture and his resumed functional-equation paragraph. The catalogue\textquotesingle s extension to P001115 must not absorb the September 1983 Deligne talk.
